title.narrative: Provision of life-saving preventive nutrition services to the most vulnerable communities in underserved and hard-to-reach rural areas of Dinsor District.

description.narrative: ltpgtOver a 12-month period, MUDRO will implement an integrated nutrition and protection program targeting vulnerable populations in ten displacement camps and host community villages in Diinsoor District. The project aims to reach a total of 10,210 individuals, including 3,000 women, 3,250 girls, 400 men, and 3,560 boys, with at least 4% of beneficiaries identified as persons with disabilities (PWD). Emphasizing equity and inclusion, the program targets internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities, ensuring no one is left behind.ltbrgtThe core intervention focuses on community-based screening for acute malnutrition among children aged 0–59 months and pregnant and lactating women (PLW), incorporating training of caregivers on family MUAC to enable early detection. This is complemented by three rounds of mass MUAC and bilateral oedema screenings conducted by trained Community Health Workers (CHWs). Identified cases will be referred to Outpatient Therapeutic Programs (OTP), Targeted Supplementary Feeding Programs (TSFP), or stabilization centers as appropriate. A gender-balanced team of 20 CHWs, trained in Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (IMAM), protection, and accountability, will conduct active case finding, referrals, follow-up, and defaulter tracing to improve treatment adherence and case management at the community level.ltbrgtComplementing treatment, the project prioritizes Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) promotion through capacity building of CHWs, formation of 50 caregiver support groups, and community mobilization. Key activities include training CHWs on counseling techniques aligned with Somalia MIYCN guidelines, quarterly cooking demonstrations emphasizing nutrient-dense complementary feeding (e.g., Tom Brown porridge) and the “One Egg Per Day” initiative, and broad dissemination of culturally appropriate behavior change communication through biannual radio sessions. These efforts aim to strengthen caregiver knowledge and practices critical to the first 1,000 days of life.ltbrgtMicronutrient supplementation and deworming form a vital nutrition-specific component, with targeted delivery of Vitamin A to 2,320 children, micronutrient powders to 1,610 children aged 6–23 months and 1,120 PLWs, and deworming treatment for 2,088 children. These interventions, supervised by nutrition officers and executed by trained CHWs, follow national protocols to address micronutrient deficiencies and reduce undernutrition risks.ltbrgtTo enhance food security and sustainable nutrition, the project will provide conditional vouchers valued at $45 to 1,000 vulnerable households in staggered tranches. The voucher package includes ingredients for fortified porridge, trays of eggs, and live chicks to support household poultry production. Voucher receipt is conditional on caregiver participation in nutrition education and community sessions, ensuring integrated behavior change alongside immediate food support.ltbrgtProtection integration is embedded throughout the project, with training on protection principles, Gender-Based Violence (GBV) mitigation, Child Protection, and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) delivered to all nutrition workers. A comprehensive complaints and feedback mechanism will engage nearly 1,000 community members, including minority and PWD representatives, enabling confidential reporting of exploitation, abuse, and exclusion. Formal agreements with community gatekeepers, incorporating PSEA clauses, will institutionalize local accountability and safeguard vulnerable populations. By combining nutrition-specific and nutrition-sensitive interventions with robust protection mainstreaming, the project will seek to sustainably improve health and nutrition outcomes for vulnerable populations in Diinsoor District. The program’s integrated approach fosters resilience, promotes inclusivity, and supports equitable access to lifesaving services for all community members, including marginalized groups and persons with disabilities.lt/pgt
